panels.title: Three traders, hidden from one another
panels.desc: Bird's-eye over the first lobe: three coastal trading posts, each screened by its own ridge, with the communal olive press on its hill between them and unlit beacons on the headland beyond.
panels.scene: High view over Paxos's north-western lobe at first light. Three small stone trading posts sit on separate hillside shoulders, each hidden from the other two by a ridge or shoulder of rock; terraces step down between them, threaded by a single winding hill track. On its own hilltop between the traders stands the great stone olive press. Further out, on twin headlands above a bay, two unlit beacon frames wait. A lone runner is already on the track, a stamped slate in his belt.

panels.title: The traders at dawn
panels.desc: Establishing panorama: the three traders on their separate hillsides, none able to see the others, a track between them.
panels.scene: Wide dawn panorama across the first lobe, a bird's-eye view no trader on the ground shares. Trader A sits on his own shoulder of hillside at left, screened by a spur of rock; Trader K is tucked into a fold of hill in the middle distance, fully hidden from A's yard; Trader M sits furthest along, behind a second ridge, hidden from both. Each has his own small sundial pillar in his yard. Low mist sits in the folds between them. A runner's path zigzags along the contour connecting all three, past the olive press on its own knoll.
panels.caption: PAXOS'S FIRST TRADERS SPOKE TO ONE ANOTHER ONLY BY RUNNER ON THE HILL TRACK — AND NO TWO SUNDIALS AGREED.

panels.title: The quarrel over the single consignment
panels.desc: At the storehouse quay: Aristides (Trader A) and Leonidas (Trader M) shout over their order slates for the single item in stock, while the wandering scholar arrives up the track behind them.
panels.scene: The stone yard of the trading post by the cove, where a single prized consignment rests under sailcloth. Aristides, Trader A, waves his purchase slate; Leonidas, Trader M, clutches the storehouse post, shouting that his order was dispatched first. Both dispute their overcast sundial readings while dock clerks back away. Behind them, coming up the last bend of the track on foot, the wandering scholar in a green himation, a satchel of scrolls over one shoulder, an abacus hanging at his belt.
panels.cast: Aristides, Leonidas, the wandering scholar, clerks
panels.caption: “I DISPATCHED MY ORDER FIRST!” “THE SUN WAS CLOUDED — MY RUNNER ARRIVED BEFORE YOUR SLATE WAS FIRED!” ENTER THE WANDERING SCHOLAR.

panels.title: Flicking the bead
panels.desc: Close-up at a trader's gate: a weathered trader flicks his abacus forward as a runner hands him a stamped clay slate.
panels.scene: Tight close-up at the gate of Trader K. A weathered trader's hand flicks a bead of his abacus forward with a thumb. A runner, sandals dusty from the track, holds out a clay slate stamped with an order and a number. The trader's other hand is already pushing his own beads past the stamped count. Terraced hillside falls away behind the gate.
panels.caption: THE LAW OF THE MONOTONIC BEAD: FLICK A BEAD FOR EVERY DEED, AND PUSH PAST THE COUNT ON EVERY SLATE YOU RECEIVE.

panels.title: Paxos's one olive press
panels.desc: At the communal press: one grower works the beam while common folk wait with baskets, each holding a wax tablet queue and a stamped slate.
panels.scene: The great stone olive press on its hill, overlooking the three coves below. One grower turns the heavy press beam while common folk wait in line with baskets of olives, each holding a personal wax tablet listing the queue of names and bead counts. A runner arrives along the track with a fresh slate, and heads turn to see whose request it carries.
panels.caption: PAXOS HAD ONE COMMUNAL OLIVE PRESS. ONLY ONE GROWER COULD USE IT AT A TIME — AND NO ONE WAS IN CHARGE OF THE QUEUE.

panels.title: Beacon across the bay
panels.desc: Night scene at the beacon headlands: cunning folk jump the queue with fire across the water while a messenger is in flight on the hill track.
panels.scene: Night across a narrow bay between two steep headlands. On the near cliff, a conspirator spots a runner's torch winding along the distant mountain pass and touches his own torch to a beacon frame, sending up a flare. On the far headland, his accomplice sees the flame and instantly dispatches a fresh request slate down to his cove's runner to jump the queue ahead of the runner still in flight.
panels.caption: A BEACON FIRE CROSSES THE BAY FASTER THAN ANY RUNNER — CUNNING FOLK JUMP THE QUEUE WHILE MESSENGERS ARE IN FLIGHT.

panels.title: The water-clock reform
panels.desc: In the counting shed by the olive press: a row of bronze water-clocks, each dripping at a slightly different rate; a clerk nudges one forward on a fresh slate, never back.
panels.scene: The counting shed built onto the communal olive press, open on one side to the hillside. A shelf holds a row of bronze water-clocks (clepsydrae), each dripping at a slightly different rate. A clerk reads an order slate just off the track and nudges one clock's float forward with a rod. A painted sign with a crossed-out backward arrow hangs on the wall behind him.
panels.caption: THE WATER-CLOCK REFORM: A CLOCK MAY BE PUSHED FORWARD WHEN A SLATE ARRIVES — NEVER BACK.

panels.title: The many-rowed abacus
panels.desc: A scribe at a lamp-lit desk with an abacus that has one row of beads per trader, copying the greater of each row from a received slate onto his own.
panels.scene: Interior close-up, no site. A scribe at a lamp-lit desk with an enlarged abacus: one row of beads for each of the three traders, each row labelled with a small painted merchant mark (a ship, an amphora, a coin). He copies the greater of each row from a received slate onto his own abacus, row by row.
panels.caption: THE LATER HAND: CARRY ONE ROW OF BEADS PER TRADER, NOT ONE IN TOTAL — AND CONCURRENCY BECOMES VISIBLE.

panels.title: The island audit
panels.desc: Across the three traders at once: clerks count vaults and cargo, runners carry slates sealed white or red, and a trader switches his own seal the instant a red slate arrives.
panels.scene: Split panorama across the three traders. At each station, a clerk counts vaults and warehouse goods. Runners on the connecting tracks carry slates sealed with either white or red wax. In the foreground, at Trader K's post, a clerk receiving a red-sealed slate is dramatically switching his own seal-stamp from white to red, the audit at his post only now beginning.
panels.caption: WHITE SEALS BEFORE, RED SEALS AFTER. THE FIRST RED SLATE A TRADER SEES, HE AUDITS HIS VAULT.
